pages.profileIntro: Identity, the public description customers see, and the contact they reach when something happens. Anchored to the ENISA TIG §5.2 supplier register and the CIR §5.1.4(d) notification chain.
pages.practicesIntro: Universal facts about how your company runs information security: management system, ISO 27001 or Grundschutz status, staff training, and the NIS 2 Article 21(2) baseline. The same answers for every customer.
pages.serviceTypeIntro: Technical declarations specific to what you provide: hosting and encryption for SaaS, SBOM and signed releases for on-premise software, background checks for professional services, PAM and on-call for managed services. Answer only the sections that apply to you.
pages.certificationsIntro: Upload your security attestations (ISO 27001, BSI Grundschutz, BSI C5, TISAX, SOC 2). The PDFs and their details are visible to the customers you have invited.
pages.customersIntro: Invite a customer by email. They get a private link to your security profile and need no account for it. Once they accept, you enter the systems you run for them and report incidents that affect those systems.

marketing.title: One security questionnaire for <blue>all your customers</blue>.
marketing.subtitle: Your customers fall under NIS 2 and have to check how securely their suppliers work. So they send you security questionnaires, each one in a different format. Here you answer the questions once and release them to every customer who invites you. <os>Open Source</os>, no lock-in.
marketing.entityDoor: Does your own company fall under NIS 2? Check applicability.
marketing.regLine: NIS 2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555 · CIR 2024/2690 · ENISA TIG v1.0
marketing.screenshotAlt: The nisd2.eu supplier portal with a completed questionnaire
marketing.step1Body: Sign in, enter your company name and domain. The profile belongs to you, not to one of your customers.
marketing.step2Body: {count} questions on security management, certification, incident plans, access, and contract clauses. Every question names the paragraph it rests on. Drafts are saved as you go.
marketing.step3Body: Each customer gets their own private link. They see your profile, the systems you run for them, and your certificates. They do not need an account.
marketing.step4Body: If a customer's system is affected, you report it from inside the portal. Only that one customer sees the report. It is how they meet their Article 21(2)(d) duty to keep an eye on their suppliers.
marketing.coversIntro: The structure follows ENISA's NIS2 Technical Implementation Guidance v1.0 from June 2025. Every question names the paragraph in CIR 2024/2690 or BSI IT-Grundschutz it rests on. An auditor recognises the structure, so you do not have to invent one. The question set is public on GitHub.
marketing.covers1Body: Legal name, address, domain, and who a customer reaches when something goes wrong. Plus the window you commit to responding in.
marketing.covers2Body: How your company runs information security: management system, certification, training, vulnerability handling, access, continuity planning.
marketing.covers3Body: Right to audit, data processing agreement, subprocessors, return of data at the end of the contract, notification of material changes.
marketing.covers4Body: SaaS, software on the customer's premises, professional services, or managed services. You only answer the questions that match your business.
marketing.covers5Body: Upload ISO 27001, BSI Grundschutz, or an equivalent as a PDF. Customers see how long it stays valid.
marketing.privacyBody: There is no public supplier directory. Only the customers you release it to can see your profile, and each of them can end their own access. No public address, no search engine indexing.
marketing.bsiQuote: Wir begrüßen aktuelle Vorstöße der Wirtschaft, einen einheitlichen Fragenkatalog für Lieferanten zu erarbeiten.
marketing.bsiQuoteTranslation: We welcome current industry initiatives to develop a unified question set for suppliers.
marketing.bsiAttribution: BSI, FAQ on NIS 2 (supply chains and security). This portal is exactly that: a unified question set, built by a company, free for anyone to use.
marketing.whyFree: The supplier portal costs nothing and the code is open. We earn from training and hands-on implementation work, not from your data. Platform and question set are on GitHub, so you can check for yourself.
marketing.footerBody: Sign in, enter your company name and domain, work through the questionnaire at your own pace. When you are ready, invite your customers.
marketing.metaTitle: NIS 2 supplier portal: one security questionnaire for all customers
marketing.metaDescription: Answer your customers' NIS 2 questions once and release the answers to every customer who invites you. Structured to ENISA TIG v1.0 and CIR 2024/2690. Open Source, no lock-in.

questionnaire.title: BSI / CIR Supplier Questionnaire
questionnaire.intro: Every question maps to a specific paragraph of CIR 2024/2690 (the binding EU regulation under NIS2) or to BSI IT-Grundschutz. Fill it once; every customer who subscribes sees the same answers.

fieldDescriptions.legalName: Your company's registered name, as it appears in the commercial register. Example: Müller GmbH or Acme Software Ltd.
fieldDescriptions.registeredAddress: Your company's registered business address. One address is enough, even if you have several locations.
fieldDescriptions.country: The country where your company is legally established. Two letters, e.g. DE for Germany.
fieldDescriptions.primaryDomain: Your main domain, usually the URL of your website. Example: acmesoftware.com.
fieldDescriptions.tagline: One line summarising what you offer. Customers see this on your supplier profile. Example: ERP for SME manufacturing.
fieldDescriptions.description: Two to three sentences about your company and what you do. This appears on your supplier profile. Sales pitch, security posture, or both.
fieldDescriptions.serviceDescription: One paragraph on what your company technically delivers to customers. Concrete products, modules, or services. Avoid pure marketing language.
fieldDescriptions.dataProcessingLocations: Every country where your customers' data is stored or processed. Comma-separated, ISO country codes. Example: DE, NL, US. If you process entirely within the EU, listing the EU countries is enough.
fieldDescriptions.securityContactName: Who customers contact when a security incident hits. In smaller companies often the managing director or IT lead. One person is enough.
fieldDescriptions.incidentContactEmail: Email address customers use to report a security incident. Ideally a distribution list like security@example.com that reaches multiple people.
fieldDescriptions.incidentContactPhone: Phone number for urgent incident reports. If you do not run 24/7 on-call, mention your business hours in brackets.
fieldDescriptions.incidentSlaHours: Hours from incident detection to customer notification, at the latest. Realistic self-assessment, not aspirational. Common values: 24, 48, or 72 hours.
fieldDescriptions.bsiRegistrationId: If your company is itself NIS 2 regulated and registered with the BSI, enter the registration ID here. Optional. Lets customers see at a glance that you meet the same obligation as a regulated entity.
fieldDescriptions.isSaas: You run software for customers on your own infrastructure and deliver it over the internet. Tick more than one box if you offer several models.
fieldDescriptions.isOnPrem: You deliver software that customers install and run on their own infrastructure.
fieldDescriptions.isProfessionalServices: Your main deliverable is human work: consulting, implementation, training, audit, or customisation.
fieldDescriptions.isManagedService: You operate parts of your customer's IT for them, with your own staff. Typical for MSP and MSSP models.
fieldDescriptions.usesAiSystems: Do your products or services process customer data through an AI or ML model? Includes external models you call through an API, for example OpenAI or Anthropic.
fieldDescriptions.hasIsms: Tick yes if you have a written information security policy with assigned roles, regular reviews, and documented incident handling. ISO 27001 or BSI Grundschutz certification implies yes.
fieldDescriptions.hasIso27001OrEquivalent: Tick yes if your company currently holds an ISO 27001, BSI Grundschutz, SOC 2 Type II, or equivalent certification. Upload the certificate in the Certifications tab.
fieldDescriptions.staffSecurityTraining: Tick yes if every staff member receives at least one annual information-security awareness training. E-learning counts; phishing simulations add to it.
fieldDescriptions.backgroundChecks: Tick yes if you run a background check for staff with access to customer data. Common bar: a criminal record extract or equivalent document on hire.
fieldDescriptions.vulnerabilityHandling: Tick yes if you have a written process for handling security vulnerabilities: detect, assess, prioritise, patch or mitigate. CVE monitoring and SLA-driven patching are the standard.
fieldDescriptions.acceptRightToAudit: Tick yes if you either grant customers an on-site audit right or provide substitute audit reports (for example SOC 2, ISAE 3402).
fieldDescriptions.hasSubprocessors: Tick yes if you use other companies to deliver your service that have access to customer data or infrastructure. Typical examples: AWS, Azure, Cloudflare, Stripe.
fieldDescriptions.subprocessorList: List every subprocessor with name, processing location, and what they do for you. A table or bullet list is enough. Update whenever you add or remove one.
fieldDescriptions.dataReturnOnTermination: Tick yes if you contractually commit to returning or destroying customer data at the end of the contract. Common practice: export and return, then delete within 30 days.
fieldDescriptions.dpaAvailable: Tick yes if you have a standard data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 that customers can sign. Required as soon as you process personal data.
fieldDescriptions.securityPolicyReviewedAnnually: Tick yes if your security policies are reviewed at least once a year and updated as needed. A written note in the document is enough evidence.
fieldDescriptions.hasIncidentResponsePlan: Tick yes if you have a written plan for handling security incidents: who decides, who communicates, who documents. At least one tabletop exercise per year is good practice.
fieldDescriptions.hasBusinessContinuityPlan: Tick yes if you have a plan that explains how you keep running or recover quickly during an outage: critical systems, fallbacks, RTO and RPO targets.
fieldDescriptions.hasCryptographyPolicy: Tick yes if you have written down which cryptography you use where: data in transit (TLS 1.2+), data at rest (AES-256), key management, hashing algorithms.
fieldDescriptions.hasPrivilegedAccessMgmt: Tick yes if administrators and privileged accounts get extra controls: separate sign-in, MFA, session logging, or just-in-time access.
fieldDescriptions.mfaEnforcedInternal: Tick yes if every internal admin or privileged account must use MFA. Hardware tokens or authenticator apps count; SMS does not.
fieldDescriptions.hasAssetInventory: Tick yes if you keep a current list of every information system you use to deliver your service: servers, databases, SaaS tools, endpoints. A spreadsheet is enough.
fieldDescriptions.hasPenetrationTestingProgram: Tick yes if you commission an external penetration test at least every one to two years. For smaller companies, an external vulnerability scan as a minimum step is acceptable.
fieldDescriptions.pastBreachesDisclosed: Tick yes if, on customer request, you openly disclose whether and which reportable security incidents your company had in the past. Common window: the last three to five years.
fieldDescriptions.incidentAssistanceCommitment: Tick yes if you commit to helping customers at no extra cost when an incident is caused by your product or service. If you agree a pre-defined day rate up front instead, also tick yes.
fieldDescriptions.cooperateWithAuthorities: Tick yes if you commit to fully cooperating with competent authorities like BSI, ENISA, or national CSIRTs during inspections, audits, and incident handling. Standard for serious suppliers.
fieldDescriptions.notifyMaterialChanges: Tick yes if you commit to notifying customers of any material change affecting your ability to deliver: acquisitions, subprocessor changes, major technical shifts.
fieldDescriptions.notifyOnLocationChange: Tick yes if you notify customers in advance before the processing location of their data changes. Important for data protection and for GDPR-compliant supply chain oversight.
fieldDescriptions.hasExitPlan: Tick yes if you have a written exit strategy: how long an orderly handover takes, what data and knowledge gets transferred, what you commit to during the transition.
fieldDescriptions.providesSbomForAi: Optional. Tick yes if you can provide an SBOM-for-AI per the G7 minimum elements (May 2026). Documents metadata, models, training data, infrastructure, security properties, KPIs, and system behaviour. Voluntary standard.
fieldDescriptions.aiSbomUrl: Public or shared URL to your SBOM-for-AI document. Can be a PDF, a JSON file, or a project page.
fieldDescriptions.saasHostingRegion: The cloud region where customer data is hosted. Example: AWS eu-central-1, Azure West Europe. Name the primary region; secondary or backup regions can be added comma-separated.
fieldDescriptions.saasEncryptionAtRest: Tick yes if customer data on disk is encrypted at rest with AES-256 or equivalent. Cloud-managed disk encryption (AWS EBS, Azure Disk Encryption) counts.
fieldDescriptions.saasEncryptionInTransit: Tick yes if all customer-facing endpoints enforce TLS 1.2 or higher. TLS 1.3 is preferred. Plain HTTP must redirect to HTTPS.
fieldDescriptions.saasMfaEnforced: Tick yes if every internal admin account on the SaaS platform must use MFA. Same standard as your internal admin policy.
fieldDescriptions.saasRtoHours: Maximum number of hours your service can be unavailable before recovery. Realistic SLA value, not aspirational. Common SaaS values: 4, 8, or 24 hours.
fieldDescriptions.onPremSbomProvided: Tick yes if you ship a Software Bill of Materials with every release. CycloneDX or SPDX are the standard formats. Mandatory under the Cyber Resilience Act for products placed on the EU market from December 2027.
fieldDescriptions.onPremSignedReleases: Tick yes if every release artefact carries a cryptographic signature customers can verify. Signing keys are documented and rotated. Sigstore or PGP signatures both count.
fieldDescriptions.onPremVulnerabilityDisclosurePolicy: Tick yes if you have a publicly documented way to report security vulnerabilities. A security.txt file under your domain (per RFC 9116) or a dedicated email like security@example.com is enough.
fieldDescriptions.onPremPatchSlaCriticalHours: Hours from public CVE disclosure to a patched release for critical vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.0+). Realistic commitment, not aspirational. Common values: 24, 48, or 72 hours.
fieldDescriptions.proServicesBackgroundCheckScope: Describe how you vet consultants for sensitive roles. Example: criminal record extract for all consultants, plus reference checks for engagements involving classified data.
fieldDescriptions.proServicesNdaInPlace: Tick yes if every consultant signs a confidentiality agreement before being assigned to customer work. Either as part of the employment contract or as a separate NDA.
fieldDescriptions.proServicesCustomerPremisesPolicy: Tick yes if you have a written code of conduct for consultants working on customer premises: badge handling, locked-screen rule, what to do if data leaves the site.
fieldDescriptions.managedPrivilegedAccessMgmt: Tick yes if you use a privileged access management tool for administrative remote sessions on customer systems. Examples: CyberArk, BeyondTrust, Teleport. A logged jump-host setup counts.
fieldDescriptions.managedSessionRecording: Tick yes if admin sessions on customer systems are recorded and retained for review. Common retention: 90 days to 1 year. Needed for forensic reconstruction after incidents.
fieldDescriptions.managedOnCall24x7: Tick yes if you operate a 24/7 on-call rotation that responds to security incidents on customer systems. Business-hours-only support does not qualify.
